items.title: Ernie Cagnolatti Interview, 1961-04-05
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I was just thinking about Jack Lane, they call him Poppa Lane, a real old-time white drummer.

ctx.x: The committees tried to make me go in that band. They said, we need men like you in that band. But I'm going to stand right here where I'm at. I was playing at the Crystal Palace with an all-day pastor at that particular time at night. And I had, I was on the WP in the day. I was doing all right. I was waiting with the commission here on Sunday. The telly order. Yeah.

I was just thinking about Jack Lane, they call him Poppa Lane, a real old-time white drummer. He's 88 now. Yeah, Poppa Lane, yeah. Yeah, yeah. People tell him something that he'd have several bands out. They say sometimes on a big day, like Carnival Day, they'd fill up bands and they couldn't, some of the guys couldn't play to put potatoes on them. So they wouldn't make any noise. They'd make them think they'd blow them and they'd act like they'd blow them.

Well, I had a bass player one carnival day. The last parade they had for the Jefferson City budget before they stopped having parades, no right, when the beginning of the war, they didn't have that other carnival. But that was the last parade. I had a band out there, I had eight pieces. The trumpet, the bass player, I had to have another band. I said, what if I don't go to another band? The people say, you know, I have all the bands, you know, cut the money. I don't really need somebody to make that money. This…
